title: Four Mechanisms of Infective Anaemia
description: Flip each card to review the key pathogen examples for each mechanism of infection-induced anaemia.

dialogs.text: Mechanism 1: Haemolysis — direct red cell destruction by the pathogen
dialogs.answer: Key examples: Malaria (P. falciparum most severe — blackwater fever from massive intravascular haemolysis), Clostridium perfringens (alpha toxin lyses RBC membranes), Bartonella bacilliformis (Oroya fever), Babesia species

tips.front: Which organisms directly invade or lyse red blood cells?

dialogs.answer: Key examples: Parvovirus B19 (targets erythroid progenitors via P antigen receptor → aplastic crisis in patients with underlying haemolytic anaemia), HIV, Leishmania donovani (kala-azar — marrow infiltration + hypersplenism), disseminated tuberculosis

tips.front: Which organisms suppress red cell production rather than destroy circulating cells?

dialogs.text: Mechanism 3: Chronic blood loss from infection-driven tissue damage
dialogs.answer: Key examples: Hookworm — Ancylostoma duodenale (commonest infective cause of iron deficiency anaemia in India), Trichuris trichiura (whipworm — heavy loads), Schistosoma species (portal hypertension leading to variceal bleeding)

tips.front: Which infections cause physical bleeding from the GI tract?

dialogs.text: Mechanism 4: Anaemia of chronic infection (ACI) — iron sequestration
dialogs.answer: Any prolonged infection triggers this via IL-6 → hepatic hepcidin ↑ → ferroportin degradation → iron trapped in macrophages → unavailable for erythropoiesis. Pattern: normocytic normochromic anaemia, low serum iron, LOW TIBC, HIGH ferritin (>100 μg/L)

tips.front: Hepcidin is the master regulator — infection raises hepcidin, which locks iron away from erythroid precursors.
